info.title: Youverify Cowork API
info.description:
Entity, Activity, Signal, Case and Workflow Management endpoints — the core Cowork platform object model. Assembled from doc.youverify.co/api-reference-sdk, endpoints kept in the exact order they appear in the GitBook navigation.

Account-wide error responses (401, 429, 500 on every endpoint; 402 on paid verification calls; 404 on lookup-by-ID calls) are sourced verbatim from Youverify's own "Youverify OS Error Codes" and "Response Codes" pages (doc.youverify.co/youverify-os-error-codes, /get-started/response-codes) and attached via components.responses, since those pages document them account-wide rather than per endpoint. Any error example that a specific endpoint's own page actually showed is kept exactly as documented there instead of being replaced by these.

post.description:
One entry point for every event type: `onboarding`, `transaction` and `account_activity` (login, card). Triggering events start evaluations; the rest are accepted and stored.

The request payloads documented here are for Transaction Monitoring (TM) events only (`transaction` and `account_activity`). There is no `externalEntityId` on the event itself: each entity identifies itself inside `data`. On a `transaction`, the sender and each beneficiary carry their own `entityId` (the Youverify platform's id) or their own `externalEntityId` (your id) with a `name` and `accountNumber`; an `account_activity` event does the same at the root of `data`; an `onboarding` event carries `data.externalEntityId` (required) and `data.entityId` (when the workflow is for an existing entity). `entityType` (`INDIVIDUAL` or `BUSINESS`) is required inside `data`: at the root of `data` for `account_activity` and `onboarding` events, and on the sender and each beneficiary of a `transaction`. Send the `entityId` whenever you have it so the event is processed and enriched faster.

**Routing.** `onboarding` (CO) is routed by `workflowId` and `workflowVersion`. `transaction` and `account_activity` (TM) carry an `eventCategory`; a login carries `data.loginMethod`, and a card event carries `data.cardAction` (`created` or `updated`).

**Triggering statuses.** Only these start evaluations: transaction `acknowledged`, `pending`; login `attempted`; card `requested`, `activated`, `pin_changed`; and `processing` for any kind. Every other status (for example `completed`, `successful`, `failed`, `issued`, `frozen`, `processed`) is stored without a run.

**Which workflows run.** Every event runs the live TM workflows tagged with its `eventCategory` whose `eventTypes` includes its type (a TM workflow must list at least one to be saved or published). An `account_activity` event runs on `{ account_activity: data }`. `eventTypes` decides which events start a workflow, not what it can read: any TM workflow can use the `behavioural_insights.*` variables, including those learned from account activity.

**Validation and idempotency.** `data` is validated per `eventType`. A transaction's `transactionReference` is its idempotency key: a repeat of one already evaluated returns the original evaluations with `replayed: true` and runs nothing (its payload is ignored even if it differs); one with no live evaluation yet runs as normal.

**Lifecycle.** An event has a `lifecycleId` only if you send one; we never generate it. An event without one is connected to no other event and adds nothing to session-risk counters.

externalEventId.description: Your own identifier for the event.

eventStatus.description: Status of the event. Only triggering statuses start evaluations; others are stored without a run.

lifecycleId.description: Optional id that connects related events. We never generate it; events without one are connected to no other event.

eventCategory.description: Category used to select the live TM workflows to run (for `transaction` and `account_activity` events).

data.description: Event payload, validated per `eventType`. Fields below are for a `transaction` event.

replayed.description: `true` when the `transactionReference` was already evaluated; the original evaluations are returned and nothing runs.
